headline: US commercial surge lifts margins, raises full-year outlook
summary_short: Palantir's Q2 2026 revenue rose 92.8% y/y to $1,935.5M, with U.S. commercial revenue up 149% y/y to $764M and GAAP operating margin reaching 47%, prompting the company to raise full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $8.150-8.158 billion.
summary_long: Q2 2026 revenue rose 92.8% y/y to $1,935.5M (+18.6% q/q), led by U.S. commercial revenue +149% y/y to $764M and U.S. government +90% y/y to $809M. GAAP operating income rose 238.6% y/y to $912.0M (47% margin); adjusted operating income rose 157.3% y/y to $1,194.5M (62% margin, Rule of 40 of 155%). GAAP net income rose 224.9% y/y to $1,061.9M ($0.41 diluted EPS, +215.4% y/y); adjusted free cash flow rose 114.6% y/y to $1,220.4M (63% margin). Cash fell 11.4% q/q to $2,030.0M; equity rose 15.7% q/q to $9,774.2M. FY2026 guidance raised: revenue to $8.150-8.158B, adjusted operating income to $4.889-4.897B, adjusted FCF to $4.5-4.7B.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: CEO Alex Karp attributed the quarter to surging demand for "AI sovereignty," with U.S. commercial revenue growth of 149% y/y and a Rule of 40 score of 155%.
Company-disclosed: driven by record U.S. commercial TCV of $2.132 billion (+153% y/y) and 220 deals of at least $1 million closed in the quarter.
Derived-arithmetic: operating margin expanded to 47% from 27% a year ago as revenue grew 92.8% y/y while total operating expenses grew only 34.2% y/y.
Derived-arithmetic: driven by cash from operations of $1,216.2 million (63% margin) against minimal capex of $14.6 million, per the release's own reconciliation table.
Not explained in the release; consistent with $3.505 billion of marketable-securities purchases during the quarter shifting cash into short-term investments.
Derived-arithmetic: growth driven by $1,061.9 million of net income plus $265.2 million of stock-based compensation added to paid-in capital during the quarter.
